ruleName: Ball moves after being put back
group: Ball moves after being put back
imagePrompt: A teenage girl kneeling on the green, watching in surprise as her ball gently rolls away after she has already replaced it and isn't near it.
imageAlt: Teen girl golfer on green, watching her replaced ball roll away before putting.

issues: The golfer is shown kneeling rather than standing, but this aligns with the prompt intent for kneeling observation.
The clothing (orange top, blue shorts), skin tone, and hat are accurate; putting green and putter are realistic.
Only one golf ball is visible with correct size and perspective.
Putter is full-length, realistic with a proper club head.

questions.title: If Your Ball Rolls Away After You Put It Back
questions.question: You mark your ball on the green, pick it up, and put it back. Before you hit your putt, the ball rolls away by itself. What should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from where it stopped
Put the ball back where it was with no penalty
Add a penalty and put it back
Go back and start the hole again

questions.explanation: If your ball moves by itself after you put it back on the green, you need to put it back where it was before. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short, smooth grass around the hole where you putt.
Extra shots added to your score if you break a rule.
Put a small coin or marker behind your ball so you can pick it up and then put it back.

questions.teachingTip: Show kids how the wind or slope can sometimes make a ball move by itself on the green, and why it's important to know what to do if this happens.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think they always have to play the ball from where it stops.
Some may think you always get a penalty when your ball moves.

questions.title: What happens if the ball rolls away after being replaced?
questions.question: After you have marked, lifted, and replaced your ball on the green, it suddenly rolls away on its own before you take your putt. What should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from its new position
Replace the ball on its original spot with no penalty
Take a penalty stroke and put it back
Start the hole over from the tee

questions.explanation: If the ball moves on its own after being replaced, you must put it back on its original spot with no penalty.
